components.css: .ds-label { color: var(--closeup-body, #2E2E2C); font-family: Switzer, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(1.0625rem, 0.95rem + 0.3vw, 1.25rem); line-height: 1.5; max-width: 22rem; } .ds-label h1 { color: var(--blume-foreground, #161616); font: inherit; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0; margin: 0; } .ds-label p { margin: 0; text-wrap: pretty; } .ds-label-medium { color: var(--blume-muted-foreground, #64645F); } .ds-label h1 + .ds-label-medium { margin-bottom: 1.25em; } .ds-label p:not(.ds-label-medium) + .ds-label-medium { margin-top: 1.25em; } .ds-label-cta { align-items: center; display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.75rem 1.5rem; margin-top: 2rem; } .ds-label-btn { align-items: center; background: var(--blume-accent, #3F3FB8); border-radius: 6px; color: var(--blume-accent-foreground, #ffffff); display: inline-flex; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; min-height: 2.875rem; padding: 0 1.375rem; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 160ms ease-out; } .ds-label-btn:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--blume-accent, #3F3FB8) 84%, var(--blume-foreground, #161616)); } .ds-label-link { color: var(--blume-foreground, #161616); font-size: 1rem; text-decoration-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--blume-accent, #3F3FB8) 55%, transparent); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.25em; transition: color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-label-link:hover { color: var(--blume-accent, #3F3FB8); } .ds-label-btn:focus-visible, .ds-label-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--blume-accent, #3F3FB8); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Step Labels
components.description: Numbered labels on the bare wall, a hairline rule on top of each.
components.html:
1. Plug in your phone. USB-C, or Wi-Fi once it's paired.
  2. Click Start Webcam. It's in the menu bar.
  3. Pick OBS Virtual Camera. In any app that asks for a camera.
  4. Tune the picture. Front or back, any lens, any way up.
components.css: .ds-steps { counter-reset: step; display: grid; gap: 2rem clamp(1.5rem, 3vw, 3rem); grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; font-family: Switzer, sans-serif; } .ds-steps li { border-top: 1px solid var(--blume-border, #E0E0DB); color: var(--blume-muted-foreground, #64645F); counter-increment: step; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.55; padding-top: 1rem; text-wrap: pretty; } .ds-steps li::before { color: var(--blume-muted-foreground, #64645F); content: counter(step); display: block; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; margin-bottom: 0.75rem; } .ds-steps strong { color: var(--blume-foreground, #161616); display: block; font-weight: 600; }

narrative.northStar: The Single Work on a Gallery Wall
narrative.overview:
Closeup's site is a quiet room. The real app, its Live Controls panel at its true size, hangs on a matte white wall under one light, and a small wall label beside it says what it is, what it needs and how to get it. Nothing else competes. The visitor reads the label the way they'd read one in a gallery: name in a heavier weight, then a few plain lines, then the one thing to do.

Density is low and type is calm. The landing page gets almost all of its hierarchy from weight and ink, not size, and the docs pages keep that voice through tokens alone: same wall, same ink, same single indigo, same light from above. Dark mode isn't a different look. It's the same gallery after hours, with a dimmer wall and a dimmer spotlight.

The world rejects the dark gradient SaaS hero, the centered headline over a device mockup, and the old warm gray type poster it replaced.
keyCharacteristics: Matte off-white wall and near-black ink, with a gray for secondary lines.
One indigo, taken from the icon's lens, only on things you can click.
One light source from above: a soft spotlight on the wall, every shadow cast downward.
Switzer for all text, Geist Mono for code.
Real screenshots at near their real size, never in device frames.

rules.name: The Lens Rule
rules.body: Indigo goes only on what acts: the Download button, links, focus and text selection. If you can't click it, it isn't indigo.

rules.name: The After Hours Rule
rules.body: Dark mode keeps every role and only dims the room. Never add a color in dark mode that light mode doesn't have.

rules.name: The Weight Not Size Rule
rules.body: On the landing page, hierarchy comes from weight and ink. The page's h1 is the same size as the sentence under it. Don't scale up a headline to make a point.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Switzer for every word you read, Geist Mono only inside code.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: There's one light and it's above. Every shadow has zero x-offset and a positive y-offset; nothing glows, nothing lifts toward the viewer on hover.

rules.name: The Hung Object Rule
rules.body: Only things hung on the wall (real app windows and panels) get a shadow, and it's a drop-shadow filter that follows the window's own transparent corners, never a box-shadow on a frame.

dos: **Do** keep Lens Indigo on things that act: buttons, links, focus, selection.
**Do** build hierarchy on the landing page with weight (400 and 600) and ink (Ink, Body Ink, Label Gray) at one size.
**Do** show the real app at its real size, lit from above with the Hung Work or Hung Figure shadow.
**Do** cast every shadow straight down, and switch the contact shadow to the 1px white rim in dark mode.
**Do** theme docs pages through tokens only and leave Blume's layout alone.
**Do** let the spotlight come up once on load and skip it under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use a dark gradient SaaS hero, a centered headline over a device mockup, or a warm gray type poster.
**Don't** add badges, chips, icon tiles or any gradient other than the spotlight.
**Don't** put a screenshot in a device frame or a box; its own corners are its shape.
**Don't** use indigo for decoration, headings, rules or backgrounds.
**Don't** add a second accent color, in either mode.
